preamble: Vocalization of the bilabial nasal [m] to schwa [ə] in unstressed syllables. In Nxa'amxcin (Moses-Columbia Salish) this 'nasal to vowel shift', first described by Kinkade (1991), is restricted to two morphemes of the shape /mix/, the imperfective suffix and the bound stem 'people'. It is conditioned by stress rather than by morphology: when the morpheme is unstressed, the /i/ is deleted, /m/ becomes [ə], and its labial feature passes to the following /x/, giving [əxʷ]; stressed forms keep [mix].

examples.note: Unstressed imperfective -mix: /i/ is deleted, /m/ surfaces as [ə] and labializes the following [x]; compare stressed kascəx̣pmíx 'It's going to burn' with [mix] intact (Kinkade 1991, cited by Willett).
Unstressed bound stem 'people'; compare stressed sq'iy'míx 'school children'.

sources: Willett, M. L. (2003). A Grammatical Sketch of Nxa'amxcin (Moses-Columbia Salish). PhD dissertation, University of Victoria, pp. 66–67. http://hdl.handle.net/1828/8056
